items.headline: Epoch Times: DOJ has not confirmed Huang's affair partner was a spy
items.summary: The Epoch Times is a right leaning paper tied to the Falun Gong movement. On Nov 12 it quoted Todd Blanche, a senior Justice Department official. He said the department has not confirmed the woman in the Nvidia affair was a Chinese spy. The headline now calls Jensen Huang the former Nvidia CEO. The woman is Alice Huang (no relation), a Chinese executive at Megaspeed, a big Nvidia customer that the Justice Department is pursuing in a criminal chip case.
items.assessment: Right wing outlets ran with the honey trap story last week. Now an official says the spy part is unproven, which cools the claim without killing it. Huang's exit means the story has already cost Nvidia its founder, so the question shifts from his loyalty to who briefed Trump and when.
items.source: The Epoch Times (headline via Muck Rack listing), context from The San Francisco Standard
items.support: Huang admitted the affair in a Sunday statement to staff. The New York Times reported Trump was briefed about a year ago and chose not to act. The Wall Street Journal reported Alice Huang is a former Chinese state TV reporter. US intelligence officials reportedly believe she gathered information for Beijing. The Justice Department took over a Commerce Department probe into Megaspeed, which bought over $4.8 billion in Nvidia chips in two years.
items.against: Blanche's own statement says the spy claim is not confirmed. China denies the allegations. The San Francisco Standard found no evidence that Nvidia caused the Megaspeed case to move to the Justice Department.

items.headline: Bannon tells his audience to stop calling the midterms stolen
items.summary: Steve Bannon, the former Trump strategist who hosts the War Room show, told viewers on Nov 7 that people should stop complaining about a stolen election. He said they must face the fact that the other side is taking the House and Senate. He still raised questions about 19 million extra voters and said the party must learn how turnout hit presidential year levels. Media Matters, a liberal watchdog, posted the clip on Nov 9.
items.assessment: The most influential MAGA broadcaster is steering away from fraud claims even as Kunstler on ZeroHedge pushes them, which splits the right's alternative media on the loss. Bannon's turnout questions keep a softer doubt alive and point the base toward a fight in Texas instead of court challenges.
items.support: Bannon cites the scale of turnout, which he says matched a presidential year. The resignation of the US attorney in Miami as a setback against what he calls the deep state.
items.against: Before the vote, Bannon called midterm polls a psyop and urged armed ICE presence at polling places, per earlier Media Matters clips. So the shift is recent. He gave no evidence that the 19 million figure reflects anything improper.

items.headline: Kucinich: 11 absent Democrats let Hegseth dodge an impeachment vote
items.summary: Dennis Kucinich, a former Ohio congressman, wrote in Consortium News on Nov 12 that the House sent Rep. Thomas Massie's impeachment resolution against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth to committee by 211 to 204. He says 11 Democrats, including Nancy Pelosi, were absent. Had they voted no, the referral would have failed and the House would have voted on impeachment itself.
items.assessment: Days after the win, the left's alternative press is turning its fire from Trump to Democratic leaders. That previews a fight over whether the new majority will use its power on the Iran war. Kucinich also wants senators to strip Section 219 from the defense bill, linking the impeachment fight to Israel policy.
items.support: The roll call absences, which he lists by name. Hegseth's own remarks at a Pentagon news conference that he personally ordered the actions covered by the articles. A No Labels study finding this House held fewer floor votes than any since 1994.
items.against: None found. No response from the absent members or House Democratic leaders appeared in our search. Absences can have personal reasons, which the piece does not address.

items.headline: New: 12 senators push to strip Israel defense integration from defense bills
items.summary: Antiwar.com reporter Dave DeCamp reported on Nov 12 that 12 senators wrote to leaders asking them to drop three provisions. Chris Van Hollen of Maryland led the letter, and Bernie Sanders signed. Sections in the House and Senate defense bills would create a US and Israel Defense Technology Cooperation Initiative for co production and joint research. A section of the Senate intelligence bill would expand intelligence sharing with Israel.
items.assessment: The fight over Israel aid is moving from the headline aid package into the fine print of the Pentagon budget, where it is harder for voters to see. The letter is the first sign the new Democratic majority's left wing will contest it before the House and Senate bills are merged.
items.support: The text of House Section 219, Senate Section 1217 and Senate intelligence Section 618. The senators' letter, which says the provisions would limit future flexibility and give Israel leverage over US weapons systems.
items.against: Benjamin Netanyahu, Israel's caretaker prime minister, calls the plan his own and says it would phase out US military aid over time. Backers argue joint research benefits US forces. No named US supporter was quoted in the piece.

items.headline: Caitlin Johnstone: AI is being shaped to recentralize control of information
items.summary: Caitlin Johnstone, an Australian independent writer, argued on Nov 12 that AI chatbots are reversing the internet's spread of power over information. She cites ADL chief Jonathan Greenblatt saying in October that his group tests major AI models and presses labs to reduce antisemitism. She also cites an academic who told an American Jewish Committee event that AI firms can be lobbied directly.
items.assessment: This is the left's version of the right's 2020s complaint about social media moderation, now aimed at chatbots. It could make AI training data a new front in the Israel debate. Expect pressure on AI firms to disclose which outside groups shape their safety testing.
items.support: Greenblatt's public remarks at a Jerusalem Post conference in Israel, Maya Ackerman's June remarks at an American Jewish Committee event. Julian Assange's 2017 and 2018 warnings that AI could steer opinion in ways people cannot notice.
items.against: The ADL describes its testing as measuring bias and hate, a role many civil rights and safety groups play with AI labs. Johnstone shows no evidence of a specific model output changed at a lobby's request.

items.headline: Drop Site: Trump calls the Iran war over but keeps the blockade
items.summary: Drop Site News, an independent outlet founded by former Intercept journalists, reported on Nov 10 that Trump called the war militarily effectively over while keeping the naval blockade. He said Gulf neighbors asked him to keep the status quo and warned a new strike would be about five times bigger. Iranian security official Mohsen Rezaei denied Trump's claim that Iran wants a deal.
items.assessment: Declaring the war over while keeping the blockade lets the White House claim peace for a lame duck Congress without giving up its main pressure tool. Citing Gulf requests also shifts responsibility for the blockade onto Riyadh and Abu Dhabi.
items.support: Trump's own public remarks, plus his claim of three aircraft carriers in the region. It also cites two tankers set on fire in Hormuz after Iran's Guards said they used an unauthorized route.
items.against: Rezaei publicly denied that Iran is seeking a deal. Fresh tanker fires the same day cut against the claim that fighting is over.
